_doc: SUBSTANCE-1 (Rowan, 2026-11-21): "Code changes end up being totally trivial. They change a hash or they change a number that should be dynamic anyway ... the illusion of productivity that absolutely must be stopped because it uses up tokens." A change is substantive only when it alters executable behaviour: after comments, whitespace, numbers and volatile strings (hashes, timestamps, dates, versions) are normalized away and import-only lines are set aside, the code tokens still differ. Consumers: foundation/substance.py (executor gate before any PR, checks backstop for executor PRs, deploy gate, 7-day report in ops/substance.json), workers/core/substance/index.js (the tick Worker classifies every merged PR so /progress and the stall alarm count only substantive changes). Both implementations pass doctrine/substance-vectors.json. Tests: tests/foundation/test_substance.py, workers/core/substance/substance.test.js.

deploy._doc: A push whose deployable change is not substantive (only regenerated data modules, ledgers or literal churn) does not redeploy the Workers unless the newest live deploy is older than max_age_hours, so regenerated counts reach the pages at most once a day instead of after every merge.

targets._doc: Measured by `python3 -m foundation substance --report` over window_days; a target out of bounds is reported by --check-targets and read by the watchdog.
